item.title: High August Swashbuckle — Sun Aug 2, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Ahoy, Ye Hearties! The Second Annual High August Swashbuckle makes landfall on Sunday August 2nd and ye be summoned! Join the crew in merriment, grog sloshing, and dancing The Hornpipe with live music from The Pubsters. Our mateys at Muddy River Distilling will be here pouring samples of their finest rums for all our old salts and carousers. And true to form, too, we’ll have delightful captain-worthy refreshments for the young lads and lassies setting sail on our voyage. Scribe ye own message in a bottle, bring color to ye favorite map, send all the rapscallion pirates to walk the plank at the Walk The Plank Dunk Tank! Dust off yer tricorn hats, strap on yer boots and show us yer best pirate swagger for a chance to win the costume contest! More treasures await! Ye needn’t any coin to attend so mark ye Ship’s Log and grab your mates – The High August Swashbuckle is here.

item.title: MST Walker Knob Overlook/Balsam Gap - Route 128, 8.5mi, 2,300ft FITNESS HIKE — Wed Aug 5, 9:30 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group One may recall how dry this trail was last time. Recent rains have returned its natural moist glory.
Car poolers will meet at the Bull Creek Valley Overlook (just past the Tanbark Ridge Tunnel) on the Parkway at 9:00am. The hike will start at the Walker Knob Overlook on the Parkway. Please let the hike leader know where you intend to meet us: carpool spot (9:00am) or trailhead (9:30am).
Any rain cancellation or venue change will be made by 7:30am.
Out and back hike. The trail elevates quickly and then undulates along a ridge of the Black Mountain chain. Expect to see lots of moss, ferns, and fungi. Some of the trail is rocky; some is soft moss and pine needle carpet.
We will stop for lunch at the Allen Rinas overlook, a rather prominent rock outcropping with a great view over the Asheville watershed (see photo) near the 4mi point, and turn around there.

item.title: The Big Asheville Science Salon! — Wed Aug 5, 5:00 PM
item.description: Welcome to the tremendous, amazing, Big Asheville Science Salon! In August: Diagnosing the Lesula monkey with evolutionary biologist Dr. James Fuller. “What’s in a name? That which we call a rose, By any other name would smell as sweet.” – W. ‘Wild Willy’ Shakespeare In a remote forest of Congo’s Lomami Basin region, researchers stumbled upon an odd looking monkey. Encountering monkeys in this part of the world is certainly not uncommon and, it’s safe to say, most are not classically handsome. But to the team of experienced field biologists, what made this particular primate peculiar was that it looked completely unfamiliar. item.title: WNC Sierra Club 8/5: Floodplains and Riverbanks Post-Helene — Wed Aug 5, 7:00 PM
item.description:
WNC Sierra Club Please join us Aug. 5 as we host RiverLink's leadership for a lively conversation about our region's flood resilience and streambank restoration efforts as we approach the two-year anniversary of Hurricane Helene. Renee Fortner and Lisa Raleigh will discuss some of the opportunities and challenges we face on our journey toward environmental and economic recovery, including examples of what we're doing well and where we're falling short amid our region's ever-changing, dynamic climate and landscape.
The program will be held both in person at the Reuter Center at UNC Asheville and [online on Zoom](https://unca-edu.zoom.us/j/85189349413?pwd=QmorsXPwjbS0BgiLR7xLItF3M1atab.1).
**Renee Fortner** is the Director of Programs at local environmental non-profit [RiverLink](https://riverlink.org/). item.title: Strawberry Gap 5.2 mi., 1,200 ft. elev. gain — Fri Aug 7, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **Sign-up opens Sunday, Aug. 2nd @ 8:00 PM**
This is a somewhat strenuous out-and-back hike, with nearly all of the uphill being on the "out" part. We'll do a moderate pace of around 2.3 mph, with breaks as needed and a 15-minute snack/water break at or near the turn-around point. It's a typical walk in the woods for these parts (which is to say, beautiful!), and the payoff at the top -- Blue Ridge Pastures -- has a panoramic view of the surrounding mountains.
***Dog Policy:*** Sorry, but dogs are officially prohibited on this trail.
***Guest Policy:*** If you'd like to bring a guest, they should join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike on their own. Alternatively, contact me in advance and ask if it's okay to bring a "+1" after you've made it onto the "Going" list. Depending on timing and demand, I may be able to add your guest.

item.title: 🌳 Better Together: The Township Tree Speaks — Sun Aug 9, 12:30 PM
item.description:
Center for Spiritual Living Asheville # 🌳 Better Together: The Township Tree Speaks
## Stories Older Than Asheville Itself
Have you ever wondered what stories a 360-year-old tree could tell? Join **Better Together** for a special outdoor gathering beneath the majestic **Township Tree**—Buncombe County's oldest known White Oak, estimated to have taken root around **1665**.
📖 **Local historian Jenny Bowen** returns to share the remarkable story behind this extraordinary tree, expanding on the history first presented during April's *Rooted in Time* dedication ceremony.
Together we'll explore: 🌿 Cherokee traditions and local legend 🛤️ The disputed Rutherford Trace campaign 🌎 Centuries of change across this land 🌳 The Township Tree's recent recognition through **Asheville GreenWorks' Treasured Tree Program**

item.title: Tool Trivia with the Asheville Tool Library — Wed Aug 12, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Power tools to power ballads – let’s wrench your brain about tools in songs, books, movies, history and MORE!
Grab your team of up to 4 and put your brains to the test across four rounds of 8 questions: songs with tools in the title, tools in movies and books, the history behind your favorite tools, and the everyday tools that actually get the job done. No tool experience required, just a love of weird facts, friendly competition, and a good pun! This is a sliding-scale, pay-what-you-can event, and every dollar raised goes directly to supporting the Asheville Tool Library: a volunteer-powered, tool-lending nonprofit with over 4,000 tools available to borrow.
